title: We don't do proposals. We do prototypes.
styleLine: ONE CONSISTENT LINE ACROSS ALL IMAGES (critical). Cinematic editorial photography, shot as if by the SAME photographer on the SAME 35mm lens, same warm natural grade — deep navy shadows (#262B38) + warm cream light (#F7F8EA), rich but natural (NOT a heavy Instagram filter, NOT washed-out, NOT HDR). A modern small software-studio workspace: walnut desks, natural window light, plants, notebooks and coffee cups, closed laptops (lids down, no visible screens). Contemporary and quiet, not corporate — a small serious team, not a coworking-space cliché. NO branded gear, NO visible UI on screens, NO stock 'business meeting' props. 4:5 (1080x1350). No text, no logos, no clearly identifiable faces (backs of heads, hands, over-the-shoulder crops are fine).
note: Craft story about Kymbo's development process — speed, no bloated proposals, show-don't-tell culture. All six slides are pure editorial photos. No composites. Companion to scene-14 and scene-20.

slides.imagePrompt: A small software-studio workspace at morning golden hour: a whiteboard with abstract non-readable sketches (boxes and lines — no text), warm walnut desk, a coffee cup, one large monstera plant. The feeling of early momentum. No people visible. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content — NO dark band, NO black rectangle, NO artificial dark area at the bottom. A CSS overlay handles text readability. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.headline:
We don't do proposals.
==We do prototypes.==
slides.sub: 48 hours from first call to a working URL you can tap through on your phone.

slides.imagePrompt: Close overhead view of hands sketching quick wireframe boxes with a pencil on blank paper, walnut desk, a ruler, a coffee cup nearby. Fast and loose — not polished design, raw thinking on paper. No readable text on the sketches. Editorial close-up. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.title: Day ==1==: we listen
slides.body: One call. You tell us the problem. We take notes on paper, not in a CRM. By the end of that call we know if we're the right fit.

slides.imagePrompt: A software-studio desk in warm side light: two closed laptops side by side on a walnut table, notebooks between them, two coffee cups, a small plant. The idea of two people working together — but no people in frame. Editorial and quiet. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.title: Day ==2–3==: we build
slides.body: Not a mockup. Not a Figma file. A working prototype on a real URL you can tap through on your phone. Ugly, fast, functional.

slides.imagePrompt: A phone lying face-down on a walnut table, a coffee cup, a notebook with a pen resting on it, warm afternoon light. The feeling of waiting for a response — the prototype has been sent. No readable screen. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.title: Day ==4==: you react
slides.body: You tap through the prototype. You say 'yes, but can it also…' or 'no, that's not what I meant.' Both answers are progress. A proposal can't give you that moment.

slides.imagePrompt: A close-up of an open notebook on a walnut desk with abstract non-readable marks — a timeline drawn as a simple horizontal line with dots along it. A pencil beside it, warm lamp light. The feeling of a plan crystallizing. No readable text. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.title: Day ==5==: we scope
slides.body: Now we know what to build. The scope comes from what you actually reacted to — not from what sounded good in a meeting room three weeks ago.

slides.imagePrompt: A fresh black coffee in a ceramic cup on a clean walnut desk, morning light, a plant in soft focus behind. Nothing else on the desk — the feeling of 'let's start.' Minimal, editorial. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.headline:
Skip the deck.
==See the thing.==
slides.sub: One call. One week. One working prototype. That's how every project starts.
